answer: Recursive Quorum Threshold. Each agent must resolve a fresh random challenge by querying a mirror set of peers whose answers must agree; the quorum widens with every concurrent identity created under one operator. An attacker cannot fake agreement, since each new identity multiplies the coordination work needed to satisfy the challenge before a sonnet of confirmations is reached. Below a dune of failed rounds, replies are rejected. Cost per identity scales with quorum size, so mass registration pays increasing compute and latency per added identity.
